x: Most of the lads are eagerly awaiting the return of Jack Brown from Cyprus. His experience will be most welcome to the newer members of our team, and his return to competitive running could well coincide with the commencement of another successful run of Belgrave performances over road and country.

We have however the prospect of the return of Jack Brown and the further improvement of many of our runners such as David Jones, Malcolm Robinson, Clive Shippen and Charlie Dabbs, plus juniors Alan Black and Ken Miller who move up to the senior ranks to inspire our hopes for 1960/61.
Mal's winning time of 4:15.8 bettered Jack Brown's nine year old mark by 2.2secs, and with six men inside 4.20 this was surely the fastest ever Club mile.
A new Club record of 13:30 set by Jack Brown on the first leg did not survive the afternoon; 30 seconds was lopped off it by Pat Newell on the 5th leg.

Amongst the runners were Ranjit Bhatia, on his last outing from Wimbledon before returning home, Jack Brown, recently returned from Cyprus and already re-establishing himself as a danger man and Cliff Roffey, home on furlough from Kenya.
Jack Brown, making a welcome return to the team, took the fourth stage to Merstham and although losing ground on the leader kept us in 2nd place.
The exception was Jack Brown, now running with much of the fire shown in his pre-Cyprus days, who moved up to 1st place on the fourth of the six stages.
Jack Brown was 21st, Charlie Dabbs (without shoes, à la Tulloh) 32nd, Masters 47th, Dooley 57th, Gebbett(recovering from gastric trouble) 60th and Johnston 64th.
Jack Brown (21.10) was also fairly well up. After these four the field became rather strung out with Hallowell, Johnson and Gebbett filling the next three positions.

Talking of the "Brighton", what a heartening sight it was to see Jack Brown handing over to Ron Linstead! The former has got back into his running most impressively after his 3 year absence whilst Ron has burst into the limelight in most sensational fashion.

Pat Newell was in a class of his own in the Senior event, with Jack Brown a good second; team support was poor however. Cyril Forey (a great prospect) was a comfortable winner of the Junior race with John Thresher third; and our Youth success was due to Hampshire and Fairclough being 2nd and 3rd.

"Evergreen" Pat Newell is running as well as ever these days and we can no doubt look forward to another consistent season from him, while Jack Brown, although getting no younger, is still likely to show a clean pair of heels to his rivals, especially when it comes to relay running.
"We've not a ghost of a chance in the National, but with a bit of luck, and if everybody turns out, we might get placed in the Southern", so said Jack Brown just after the Club '10'.
Jack Brown had the place of honour, but despite the excellent time of 17.53 could do little more than gain on all the teams ahead except Woodford.
Held on March 4th, two weeks before the Ilford, the Bels. got off to a great start when Jack Brown came home a clear leader on the first stage.
Held on March 25th, this was the club championship race for the "Wimbledon" Cup, and Jack Brown was the name to be inscribed under that of Ramjit Bhatia - who set such a hot record last year.

STAGE 8 - Jack Brown (30.25, 10th fastest). Jack protests that he is getting old, but there are few in Belgrave who can hold him on the road; as he proved by lowering Charlie Dabbs stage record by 18 seconds to maintain our sixth position in the face of heavy opposition.

His 8.55 when placed third in the London Club's 2 mile race at the White City erased Jack Brown's mark of 8.59 from the record book. Others to set up personal bests in this event are Malcolm Robinson with 9:08.2, Pat Newell 9:09, Dan Maclean 9:11.6 and John Davies 9:15.
In the A.A.A. 10 miles track championship, held at Hurlingham on 15th April, Jack Brown finished 4th in 51 minutes 11.8 seconds - just 0.8 seconds outside Charlie Dabb's club record.
Jack Brown, who has won this trophy on four consecutive occasions, made every effort to close the gap, but halving it was the most he could manage and so had to be content with second place.

On the third leg, Jack Brown maintained our place with an excellent 13:36, and although he was the "A" team's slowest man, John Thresher (14:09) ran well enough to take us up to second, 43 secs. behind the eventual winners - Polytechnic Harriers.
Jack Brown made a valiant effort to keep the gap as small as possible between himself and the loping Scot ahead, but Bill seemed to have the matter well in hand at all times.

STAGE 8 - Jack Brown (31:50. 15th) Jack took over still in 6th place but 3½ mins. behind Portsmouth. Jack was obviously not at his best, and although plugging along on what is the hardest stage of all, was noticeably losing ground on all teams ahead.

Elsewhere in this Gazette a spotlight has been thrown upon the career of that fine athlete Jack Brown. This was prepared on hearing of Jack's retirement, but he has since told me that the urge to compete again is very strong.
The mid 1920s were not the most pleasant years that this country has known and Jack William Brown was born in 1925, a year before the General Strike.

Eric Gebbett (A) Jack Brown (B) and Ray Conway (C) set off on the first stage and eyebrows were raised when Jack and Eric came down the finishing straight together in 6th and 7th positions - a fine start for both teams.

Pat now holds two Club stage records against Jack Brown's three - this can surely be changed next April Pat! The story of the race is one that almost excludes the winners Portsmouth for they took the lead on the third stage and from then on it was only a question as to how far ahead they would be at Brighton.

TOP LEFT: Eric Gebbett fights out the first stage against Fudge (Portsmouth) and Darbon (Shaftesbury). TOP RIGHT: Jack Brown climbs the airport drag on Stage 3. CENTRE LEFT: Cyril Forey on the Gatwick stage.

Cambridge Road as usual, sorted the sheep from the goats and Barry Sawyer returning once more to the form he showed about a year ago, pulled away from Eric Gebbett and Jack Brown who were renewing the battle they enjoyed in the Poly Relay only a week before.

New faces are always welcome and this season the road running ranks have been swelled by Gerry North, Bill Kerr, Charlie Walker, George Williams John Moore and Peter Wrench; and with Jack Brown showing a return to form, things look good for next season.

Jack Brown had to make full use of his experience to pull back Tony Fairclough and John Davies in the later stages but eventually he got away from them and was fast catching Barry Sawyer in the run in.
But Gerry is a champion and held off last year's winner by 10 yards to provide an even more exciting finish than when Jack Brown pulverised Dennis O'Gorman a few years back.

Jack Brown, who appeared only as a reserve, was a gallant 109th in his first race since the Club '7' in early December. Close behind was Don Maclean (118) who made ground impressively in the latter stages to complete our scoring six.
He works at the War Office where he occasionally teams up with that other Belgrave stalwart Jack Brown in their sports club team. How good it is to see Charlie Dabbs running well again.
Charlie Walker had a good run to give us the lead, 3 seconds ahead of Chelmsford (Hill-Cottingham) and Jack Brown increased this to 14secs with Poly (Proffitt) moving up to second place.
Walker, Jack Brown, or any of his contemporaries they'll tell you that he was one of the closest 'near-misses' that British athletics has had.
In the A.A.A. 10 Mile Track Championships at Hurlingham, Jack Brown finished 9th in 52:26.4 (Intermediate times. 3 miles 15:28.0; 6 miles 31:14.0).

A "ghost" Belgrave team ran in the Wimbledon '10' on the day of the Southern London-Brighton relay and finished 10th. Jack Brown was 27th in 55:18 Norman Stairs 36th in 56:17, Pete Sadler 38th in 56:23 and Bob Glover 46th in 57:12.
Barrie Sawyer regained the lead on the 3rd leg with a good run and this was maintained by Jack Brown, Trevor Hart and Arthur Bruce on legs 4, 5, and 6.
Next to take over was Jack Brown, but not surprisingly he had to give way to 'kipper' Herring who pulverised the opposition, and took Blackheath from 7th into a 100 yard lead.

Jack Brown was 9th in the A.A.A. track '10' at Hurlingham on April, 11th, recording the good time of 54:18.4. At the Herne Hill Winter Floodlit meeting at Totting Bec on March, 25th, John Thresher won the 3,000 metres in 8.37.0 and Danny Wiseman the 660 in 82.7.

With the main pack throughout, he finished strongly just ahead of Jack Brown who is always able to shake up his younger opponents. Mike's improvement is the deserved result of 2 to 3 years of hard conscientious work and his progress will be followed with interest.

With a tremendous effort Gerry took all but 10 seconds off the Pompey runner (Wale) and, although we failed to win, we were able to furnish our last leg runner in the "Brighton" (Jack Brown) with some interesting facts about his probable opponent!

Although Jack Brown (back into the team again after missing a number of Brightons) was our oldest runner;his great experience soon became apparent,for against a Portsmouth newcomer on his first Brighton, he closed the gap rapidly.
Jack Brown ran himself back into the Brighton team in convincing fashion and Bicourt, in only his second crack at the event, showed he will be well to the fore next time.

Despite fine efforts by Gerry North(4th),John Thresher(8th),Geoff.North (14th)and Jack Brown(30th)Belgrave failed to win the team race by the narrowest possible margin- 1 point.Belgrave scoring 56pts to Surrey AC's 55.
Jack Brown and Mike Shingles also ran well to finish 7th and 10th respectively,but we still only managed 2nd team behind Maidstone who packed 3,4 and 5.

Belgrave's Jack Brown was next reserve on call and would certainly not have done worse than this supporting cast. His absence from the race also meant that the Club had gone 9 years without gaining an international vest over the country.

The most impressive runs were by Adrian Major, a youth, and by Jack Brown, almost a veteran. Adrian's relentless pace took him thro' to sixth-fastest time of the day, whilst Jack showed a fine turn of speed to hold off scratch men Black and Hart.

Only 7 of our Brighton 12 were running but they finished well enough up to take our scoring 10 to a narrow win. Jack Brown followed up his memorable relay effort with a fine 17th place,only 17secs behind Tony Fairclough (18 years his junior).
Jack Brown also ran well and will no doubt be picking up many Vets prizes come his 40th birthday in August. John Dear,Don Maclean and the "Dukes Joggers" completed our two teams. 153 finished.

Mike Shingles, who had been below his best for several weeks, was unable to break through the spell and dropped us to 4th on the next stage- a position maintained by Jack Brown on the 3rd leg, and who regained much lost ground in closing up to within 13secs of the runner ahead.

Only 4 of our expected six appeared and Jack Brown and Don Maclean were moved up to fill the gap. Both ran very well, but we were obliged to concede 53 seconds to Blackheath at the end and had to be content with 3rd place.

Trevor Hart ran well on the Redhill stage and kept his place, although losing a little ground on Coventry, and when Jack Brown (40 this year!) took over on the short leg Coventry were only 37 seconds ahead.
Jack Brown showed the rest of the field a thing or two, beating his old rivals Newell and Walker and dusting up those young "upstarts" Bicourt, Dear and Major!

Of the others Doug Brew ran very well in his first attempt at the distance to finish in 67th place. Mike Bullivant broke Jack Brown's course record by over a minute but it should be remembered that conditions were ideal.

…shing behind 20 years old Reilly was a runner exactly twice Joe's age - that elder statesman of the running fraternity, Jack Brown. Jack moved well away from his immediate rivals on the final lap and clocked a time that placed him 5th in the handicap - form that suggests he will be running yet again…
Their last man was few places in front of Charlie Walker - perhaps Jack Brown may have a twinge of conscience for withdrawing just to let Charlie run !
It was good to see Ranjit Bhatia showing some of his old form again and with Jack Brown and Pat Newell also putting in useful appearances the team was not unlike those of 7 or 8 years ago.

Once again veteran Jack Brown put in another of his stirling performances, shaking up many first team aspirants with his 29:27; and Ranjit Bhatia made the most of his years stay in England by re-appearing in the race for which he once held the record (27:56 in 1960).
Overheard in the dressing room:- "The reason that Jack Brown remains so fit is that his son is now running so well over half a mile that Jack has to make sure he doesn't beat him!
Jack Brown went through the field like a dose of salts with 3 mile splits of 15:40 and 15:31 to beat Ranjit Bhatia who was competing in his last track race before leaving again for India in October.
His struggling effort left him over two minutes behind our first man, Peter Whewell, and dangerously near that old Belgrave favourite, Jack Brown.
Also to Chas Walker, over 9 mins faster than his time last year - what would he do if he started training again !! (Jack Brown please note !!!)
North takes the platform on "Timekeeping today". Jack Brown speaks on "Putting back into athletics what you get out".
Jack Brown

This was the match we've been waiting for, a 5 Mile cross country race at Hayes against the veterans of Blackheath with the added interest of the meeting between Jackie Brown and Charlie Walker brought together for the first time as Vets by the Cross Country Secretary through devious means known only to himself.

JACK BROWN is alive and well and winning mile races! Our star of yesteryear, who was in international class at everything from one to twenty miles, raced in the event at which he started out when competing in the veteran's mile at the Carshalton Trophies meeting in April.
Taking the lead, which he held to the end, is Len Marchant who won in 1:59.0 from Len Herbert (4th from right) and Jack Brown (6th from right).
He followed this up by beating all the juniors for the 'Savage Shield', beating all the seniors, bar Jack Brown, in the 'Blackstaffe Shield' seven miles, and finishing 2nd in the Surrey Youths.

The individual winner was Bill Lucas, and he finished full of running, and was followed home by Chas. Walker and Jack Brown. Mick Porter and Lew Bush also ran well as did J.H.Braggington, who is a first season runner over the country.

In the over 50 event 2nd claim member Jack Brown (Cambridge H) was the winner in 36:13. The Belgrave team scored 61pts for 7th place with E.Young 23rd in 41:23, Joe McDonald 31st in 42:26 and John Baker 44th in 43:47.
In the Club Championships of 1955 he ran in the 1 mile and clocked 4:27 for 3rd place behind Jack Brown's 4:23. Brian Hallowell, who was to become John's training partner and rival, placed 2nd.

We had triangular matches with Herne Hill H and Woodford Green AC and in the Senior 100 yards we saw Holtum finishing 3rd, and he followed this with a 4th in the 220. Badiali was 3rd in the 440 and Jack Brown finished 2nd in the 880 with Bob Taylor in 4th place.

In the Club Championships at Battersea Park Jack Brown came over from the White City where he had been running for the Great Britain "B" team in an attack on the 4 x 1 mile world's record, and he successfully defended his 1 mile title, beating Chas.

In 1949 the first two men home, Vernon Blowfield and Jack Brown went slightly off course and were effectively disqualified but Verne took the record down to 29.09 in 1950, and following the cancellation of the 1952 race through snow bound roads, Ray Tooby opened up the 28 minute era with 28.50 in 1953.

We did, however, have Jack Brown in 6th place in the Kent Championship. This situation was confirmed a few weeks later in the Inter-Counties, our first scorer in 52nd place being Bill Lucas - Surrey's third man.
The Club Ten Mile Championship following the Counties was won by Jack Brown from Charlie Walker and Bill Lucas, confirming our hopes for the big races ahead.

On the next stage to Merstham, Ted Stimpson held his place ... then Frank Abberton tackled the uphill stage through Redhill and ran a fine race to take us up to 2nd place. On the next stage Jack Brown took us in front.

I well remember a very agitated Jimmy Green (Editor of Athletics Weekly) running up to me saying 'There's an unknown runner up ahead running in an un-numbered white vest. He took over from Jack Brown so he must be one of your's.
This was followed by 3rd in the Southern and 6th in the National with the lead man on each occasion being Jack Brown with Charlie Walker, Len and Alan Bishop, along with Dennis Brickwood in the team.
Bob Taylor equalled the Middlesex record held by the great Arthur Wint in the 880 yards, and Ivan Mayers beat Ron Holtum in the sprints while Jack Brown won the Kent one mile.
The year started with the road runners winning the Mitcham 15 led by the individual winner Jack Brown. Then followed a third place in the Southern race at Epsom.
